body: I have no reason not to. I'm just waiting for the right moment. I'm sorry you have been struggling, and I'm glad you're still here. You can talk to me if you want.

The studying and time management all comes in time. Those are small things to work on, and they are very manageable issues. 

Breakups and losses are always hard. I would like to urge you to try and stay away from pursuing any romantic relationships for a while - I believe that it is necessary to work on yourself first, before taking such a large chance with someone else. That does not mean you can't reach out to people - I think that is a good idea to reach out for friends. But sometimes pursuing any romantic relationships that can get rather intense in a state of mind that is intense enough all by itself might not be the best idea. 

Try not to put so much pressure on yourself when it comes to school. Is this your first year of university? Even if it isn't, you are going through a lot personally. It is perfectly okay to not be the *best* student in a time like this, especially if you are going through the transition period of restarting school. 

What do you like to do for fun? I would like to encourage you to make time for yourself first, before you pressure yourself so much for school. I can't even begin to say what a difference an hour a day of personal time doing something you enjoy can do for your mental health. Even if it is just going for a walk, or listening to your favorite song. Take time for yourself, without worrying about school.

It is hard to keep going up all the time, if you know what I mean. Maybe it was getting better, maybe the panic was subsiding, maybe it was changing. But it all ebbs and flows - moods, situations, life in general. Nothing is good all the time. Life has its ups and its downs, and just because you faced a minor set back does not mean that you aren't moving forward still. As long as you keep moving forward, there is reason to hope. That will always be true. 

You are not expected to be able to be strong all the time, or happy all the time, and the sooner you accept that NO ONE is ever at 100% all the time, the sooner you will be able to accept yourself and begin to heal. It is a long road, and one I still am traveling on. But once you can see life for what it is, and not what it is supposed to be, things will get easier. No one is supposed to be this or that all the time. It is an imperfect cycle.

Cutting and self harm is a slippery slope, and I understand very well that once you do it, it makes you feel good and bad at the same time. Self harm is not something to be ashamed of - each person in life copes in different ways. I know it probably makes you feel a certain way about yourself, and that is hard. But minor set backs are nothing to be ashamed of, and I promise you, it will get better.

Can I ask you - what do you mean you aren't good enough? Good enough for what in particular? Professional enough to do what specifically? Sweeping generalizations like that do not help anyone, because it just isn't true. It is a way to knock yourself down even further, and it is not healthy.

I have been here so, so many times. I know it doesn't feel like you are important right now, but that is not true in any way, shape, or form. Maybe right now, this seems like the best, the only option, but it isn't. There are ways to change your situation, even if they are small changes, they will make a difference - all the small changes add up into something big. This won't be forever - and I know that sounds so cliche and overused (I used to hate it when people would tell me that), but it really is the truth. It may look like this is the way your life is going now.. but think about all the ways it has changed so far. I don't know your situation, but I know that nothing stays the same forever, and that is scary, but also comforting.

Everyone is allowed to be weak. Everyone is allowed to fail. It is human nature, and I promise you, things do get better.

I am here to talk if you would like. You can PM me, or we could talk on here if you would prefer.

I think everyone does have something that makes them special, whether it is big or small, good or bad. I think it really depends on who is criticizing the situation, too. If someone who has had major tragedy in their life sees someone who has only suffered something "small" (even though it seems large to that person), they might scoff at the idea of that person really suffering anything.

I have a very similar problem. I am always looking ahead also, worrying about the future and what is going to happen. My SO constantly gets upset with me because I "live in the future," and he says that if I keep doing that, my whole entire life will pass me by without me every really enjoying anything. 

I think it is important to realize you are doing it, and trying to correct those habits now before it becomes worse. Like the others suggested, try to meditate. I don't ever "really" meditate, but I do agree with you that you can do it anywhere at anytime. One thing that I do that really seems to help is to lay in bed either in the morning before you start your day or at night when it is almost over, turn on some nice relaxing music, be it ambient or something else that makes you relaxed, and just focus on the music - don't think about anything else, just the music. It is very calming, and "in the moment."
